title: Awei-5 protects against posterior circulation ischemic vertigo by modulating oxidative stress and the HIF-1alpha/VEGF.
authors: Yang, Yuqiu; Chen, Zhixin; Zhao, Fuquan; Pang, Yuxin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究传统蒙药Awei-5对后循环缺血性眩晕的神经保护作用，聚焦氧化应激与HIF-1alpha/VEGF通路，分子对接仅用于验证药物成分与靶蛋白结合，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合位点预测或互作机制建模，且方法以实验为主，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Awei-5 (AW-5) is a classic Traditional Mongolian Medicine formula with a centuries-long history. It has traditional functions of activating blood circulation and treating 'Head Heyi' (Wind-stroke). Clinically, it is widely used for vertigo and posterior circulation ischemic vertigo (PCIV), though its molecular mechanisms remain elusive. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to identify the bioactive components of AW-5 and investigate its neuroprotective effects and underlying molecular mechanisms against PCIV using an integrated pharmacological strategy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-Q-TOF/MS analysis and Network pharmacology were employed to screen active components and predict core targets. A rat PCIV model was established to evaluate neuroprotection via behavioral tests, Nissl staining, and oxidative stress assays. The regulation of the HIF-1alpha/VEGF pathway was assessed through immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting, followed by molecular docking verification. RESULTS: Network analysis identified the HIF-1 signaling pathway as a core therapeutic target. In vivo, AW-5 significantly alleviated behavioral deficits and neuronal damage. It effectively mitigated oxidative stress by reducing MDA levels and restoring SOD and GSH-PX activities. Furthermore, AW-5 significantly upregulated the mRNA and protein expressions of HIF-1alpha and VEGF, promoting an adaptive angiogenic response. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities between key AW-5 ingredients and HIF-1alpha. CONCLUSIONS: AW-5 exhibits significant neuroprotective potential against PCIV by suppressing oxidative stress and activating the HIF-1alpha/VEGF pathway to facilitate angiogenic repair and neuronal survival. This study provides a solid scientific basis for its traditional clinical application, offering promising avenues for novel therapeutic strategies and drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：阿魏-5（AW-5）是一种经典的传统蒙药方剂，拥有数百年的应用历史。其传统功能包括活血化瘀及治疗“头赫依”（中风）。临床上，它广泛用于眩晕及后循环缺血性眩晕（PCIV），但其分子机制尚不明确。研究目的：本研究旨在通过整合药理学策略，鉴定AW-5的生物活性成分，并探讨其针对PCIV的神经保护作用及潜在分子机制。材料与方法：采用超高效液相色谱-四极杆-飞行时间质谱（UPLC-Q-TOF/MS）分析和网络药理学筛选活性成分并预测核心靶点。建立大鼠PCIV模型，通过行为学测试、尼氏染色和氧化应激检测评估神经保护作用。通过免疫组织化学、实时定量聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）和蛋白质印迹法评估缺氧诱导因子-1α（HIF-1alpha）/血管内皮生长因子（VEGF）通路的调控，随后进行分子对接验证。结果：网络分析确定HIF-1信号通路为核心治疗靶点。在体内实验中，AW-5显著改善行为缺陷和神经元损伤。它通过降低丙二醛（MDA）水平并恢复超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）和谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶（GSH-PX）活性，有效缓解氧化应激。此外，AW-5显著上调HIF-1alpha和VEGF的mRNA及蛋白表达，促进适应性血管生成反应。分子对接证实AW-5关键成分与HIF-1alpha之间具有强结合亲和力。结论：AW-5通过抑制氧化应激并激活HIF-1alpha/VEGF通路以促进血管生成修复和神经元存活，展现出针对PCIV的显著神经保护潜力。本研究为其传统临床应用提供了坚实的科学依据，为新型治疗策略和药物发现提供了有前景的途径。
